correctness.rationale: For each finite-forest downset algebra B, the new-root construction gives n(H)=n(B)+1, sigma(H)=n(B)+1+sigma(B) and Delta(H)=n(B)^2-sigma(B); products multiply sigma and satisfaction counts. Structural induction proves sigma(H)<=n(H)(n(H)+1)/2 with equality precisely for chain duals. This yields Delta(H)>=(h-1)(h-2)/2 on rooted trees and the sharp global one-ninth gap with all equality cases. Brute-force verification directly computes implications for every increasing forest through seven vertices (5913 presentations), including all boundary and equality checks. Infinite claims rest on proof, not these tests.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a sharp finite satisfiability gap for a standard classical principle in finite Gödel–Dummett algebras even though unrestricted finite Heyting algebras have no such gap, addressing a restricted-class direction explicitly motivated in Bumpus–Kocsis §6.6. It characterizes all sharp extremizers and derives a stronger sharp bound for every connected tree-dual algebra size. The implication-fixpoint counting lemma gives a structural reason for the constant, not just finite experiments.
